newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Strength spills over into April.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Strength spills over into April.

text.p: The recent strength in gas oil and jet fuel prices which was seen for March cargoes has now spilled over into April as a local trader continued to buy barrels for the new month, traders said on Wednesday.
While April gas oil cargoes were traded below $27.00 per barrel on Tuesday, the trader on Wednesday bought a 150,000-barrel cargo for April 6-10 lifting at $27.10 from a Dutch trader.
But a Mediterranean trader appeared to be resisting the rise, selling to the local trader an April 3-7 cargo at $26.45, which was below the deal on Tuesday.
An end-March cargo was purchased by the trader from a Thai trader at $28.00, up 20 cents from Tuesday.

With the latest purchases, the the local trader has bought a total of over 2.0 million barrels of physical gas oil cargoes within a span of less than two weeks. Traders said the cargoes were required to fill a VLCC which is now ready for shipment.
The trader concerned said he might buy more gas oil to fill two more VLCCs, something which other traders said is not impossible.

But traders said China recently bought a 30,000-tonne cargo of gas oil at $191.50 per barrel on a free-on board basis from South Korea. This is $27.50 per barrel fob, which is way below current traded levels for end March or early April lifting cargoes.

Jet fuel prices were held steady when the Singapore trader bought a total of 200,000 barrels in two cargoes from a European major. The trader bought a March 27-31 lifting cargo at $28.70, up 10 cents from Tuesday, and an April 5-9 cargo at $27.50, the same level as Tuesday's deal.
But traders noted that the rally on gas oil has narrowed the swaps jet/gas oil regrade to be offered at $1.00 from Tuesday's $1.30 for March. April regrade was $0.50/$0.70, from Tuesday' $0.80/$1.00.

Traders noted that the jet fuel market was in steep backwardation as seen in Taiwan's purcahse of one to two late April delivery cargoes at over $212 per tonne, cost-and-freight basis, down from March delivery cargoes.
Demand for gas oil and jet fuel has emerged from Sri Lanka which has issued an import tender for a combination cargo for April 11-12 delivery, closing March 18.
